theory.intro: **Float time** is how long an activity can be delayed without delaying the activities that follow it. Once a forward and a backward scan are done, it is read straight off the boxes at the two ends of the activity's edge.
facts: The EST comes from the left box at the vertex where the activity starts.
The LST comes from the right box at the vertex where the activity ends.
An activity with a float time of $0$ is a **critical activity** and cannot be delayed at all.
An activity with a positive float time is **non-critical** and can be delayed by up to that many time units.
Delaying a critical activity by one time unit delays the whole project by one time unit.
A dummy activity has duration $0$, and its float time is found in exactly the same way.
steps: Read the EST from the left box at the vertex where the activity starts
Read the LST from the right box at the vertex where the activity ends
Subtract the activity duration and the EST from that LST
Call the activity critical when the float is 0, and non-critical otherwise
